name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya
blurb: A domed Victorian-era building with a long, well-lit gallery. Ninety minutes covers the ground floor without rushing it.
description: The main hall is a single long room with good daylight and benches, which is unusual for a museum this size. Rooms off it go deeper on Maratha and pre-Maratha material, and you can feel the temperature drop. Wheelchair users are set up at the entrance; upstairs galleries have lifts but the approach is fiddly.

activities: looking at the arms and armour

__meta.note: `accessibility.hearingLoop: true` is an inferred estimate so the compound-need eval scenario is testable. Unverified.

name: Jehangir Art Gallery
blurb: Maharaja-built, one flat gallery, and a courtyard sculpture garden that is the better half. Closed Mondays.
description: Two long rooms and a sculpture garden with a fountain, run as a charity for blind and low-vision artists. The garden is level, planted, and quiet, which is the part that works with a wheelchair or a pram. The main hall has a step at the entrance and a ramp to one side.

activities: looking at modern and folk work

__meta.note: Entry arrangements change; `pricePerPerson` is null here (treated as free) and is a demo assumption.

name: David Sassoon Library
blurb: A polychrome Victorian reading room, a yellow-and-red house on a hill, and air conditioning that is colder than you expect.
description: A public reading room on a working library building, with a painted ceiling and a long shared table. Free to sit, and the room itself is worth the walk up the steps. Flat throughout; the counter at the entrance is high and there is a lift to the upper floor.

name: National Gallery of Modern Art, Mumbai
blurb: Three floors of post-Independence Indian painting. A lift to every level, which is genuinely rare in the Fort.
description: A converted residence turned museum, with M.F. Husain, Raza, and Amrita Sher-Gil across three floors, and a sculpture court at the top. Small enough that an hour is plenty. Level access to the ground floor, lift to the rest, and a hearing loop at the counter.

activities: a lift to the top floor

name: Flora Fountain
blurb: Cast iron, an octagonal fountain, and a traffic island. Twenty minutes at most, and it is a genuine shortcut.
description: A cast-iron fountain on a junction, sculpted figures, and a ring of steps people sit on. Standing on a road island means traffic, so it is a place to photograph rather than linger. Level from the pavement, open all night, and a useful mid-plan pause.

activities: sitting on the steps for a minute

name: Wadia Clock Tower
blurb: A clock on a tower on a busy corner. Fifteen minutes, and it is on the way rather than a detour.
description: A 1914 clock tower on Veer Nariman Road, still running, with a road going round it. You do not stop here, you pass it. Useful for a plan that needs a fifteen-minute honest filler, or a landmark to give directions by.

name: St. Paul's Church, Fort
blurb: An 1860s Gothic Revival church with a rusted, riveted iron roof, and a graveyard worth ten minutes on its own.
description: One of the oldest buildings in the Fort, restored, with a corrugated iron roof on an iron frame and a graveyard behind. Services on Sunday mornings; outside that it is locked and you look through the grille. Four steps up and a hard threshold, so the graveyard rather than the nave is the accessible half.

name: St. Anthony's Church, Fort
blurb: The church that survived the Blitz, on a lane behind the office blocks. Small, tiled, and usually open.
description: A working church that came through the 1944 bombing largely intact, which is why it still has its fittings. Open through the day on weekdays, with a porter at the door. Three steps and a narrow aisle; the side chapel is level once you are in.

name: Bhau Rangaji Temple
blurb: An 18th-century Ganapati temple in a lane, still on a working street, with a bell and a tulsi plant.
description: Small, tiled, and hemmed in by buildings on three sides. The bell is rung by hand. Sleeveless tops and shorts are a problem at the doorway, which is worth knowing before you walk in. Three steps to a small dark room.

name: Minara Masjid, Mohammed Ali Road
blurb: The striped red-and-white mosque at the north end of Mohammed Ali Road, with a minaret you can see from four streets away.
description: Red and white bands, a tall minaret, a broad courtyard, and the street food market outside the gate after sunset. Non-Muslims are welcome in the courtyard. Steps at the main entrance, with a side ramp; shoes off at the door, so a bag of footwear is unavoidable.

name: Dongri to Dubai
blurb: A lane of wood-carvers, brass workers, embroidery frames and a car-worship place at the end. Squeeze through, then look up.
description: A working craft lane where you buy nothing and watch everything. The wood carvers and the copper workers are two doors apart, and the car-worship at the far end is a building you should not walk into. Pavement is narrow and broken, so a pram is hard work. Closed Sunday.

name: Chor Bazaar
blurb: Second-hand everything, three aisles deep, with a bridal section on top that nobody expects. The stairs are the problem.
description: Furniture, brass, records, and a top floor that sells wedding goods — the building is best known for the upstairs, and it is the least interesting floor. The staircases are steep and turn. If you cannot do stairs, this is the one Fort market that is worth skipping, and the engine should say so rather than send you into a stairwell.

name: Crawford Market
blurb: Iron-and-glass, a fruit section at one end, and a wholesale crowd that turns chaotic before ten. Lift to the second floor.
description: A Victorian iron market hall with a curved roof and a working wholesale trade behind the retail frontage. Level throughout on the ground floor, with a public lift or a ramp to the upper gallery. Toilets on site. Best before ten or after four; the middle of the day is a wall of people.

activities: using the lift to the gallery

name: RBI Monetary Museum
blurb: Free, nearly always empty, and you can hold a 22-karat gold bar. Four rooms in an old stone building.
description: A small central-bank museum in a nineteenth-century building: coinage, currency, and a gold display where staff will bring out a bar for you. Free, small, and the kind of place children like because there are objects to hold. There is a step at the entrance and a lift to the upper floor.

name: Knesset Eliyahoo Synagogue
blurb: A 1884 synagogue on a lane behind the Kala Ghoda temples, with hand-painted ceiling panels and no crowds at all.
description: Baghdadi Jewish, built in the 1880s, restored, and open to visitors with a caretaker on the premises. The painted ceiling and the bimah are the reason to go. Level access through the gate on the side lane; closed for Jewish holidays, and the gate is locked without notice.

__meta.note: Closed for Jewish holidays. Check before travel; not modelled in `hours`.

name: Novelty Theatre
blurb: Marathi and Hindi plays in a 133-year-old theatre on a back street, with a balcony you can actually reach by lift.
description: An old working theatre doing new plays in Marathi, in English, and in Hindi, with a matinee on Sunday. Cheaper than a cinema and a completely different kind of evening. The upper circle is up a staircase; the stalls are level and the lift reaches the circle, which is the unusual part.

name: Metro INOX, Fort
blurb: A 150-year-old marble and wrought-iron cinema with recliners and a food court. It eats a whole afternoon on its own.
description: A restored single-screen cinema in a marble building, with a food court in the old lobby and recliner rows. It is the reason several people plan a Fort afternoon, and the reason nobody should put it in a two-hour window. Step-free from the street, hearing loop at the box office, toilets on site.

name: Alliance Française de Bombay
blurb: A 1930s art deco school with a courtyard, a library you can walk into, and a cafe that is open to everyone.
description: An art deco institution in a restored heritage building, with a small library, a courtyard, and a cafe that does not require enrolment. Free to use the library and courtyard during opening hours. Lift to the upper floor, hearing loop in the auditorium, toilets on site.

activities: a free talk if one is on

name: Maharashtra State Archives
blurb: Eighteenth-century records in a strongroom, retrievable on request for a fee. Bring photo ID and expect to wait.
description: Maharashtra's pre-1947 government records: revenue rolls, maps, and correspondence, in a strongroom on a Fort lane. You ask for a box, they retrieve it, and you read it in a supervised room. A staircase and a lift with a cage door. Bring ID; the fee is small but it is not free.

name: Chandni Chowk food lane
blurb: Awadhi kebabs and mithai on a lane that is only interesting after seven. Sit on the plastic chairs if you get there before nine.
description: A lane of kebab and mithai shops that fills after dusk, with plastic seating that runs out. Late, loud, meat-heavy, and genuinely good rather than convenient. Pavement is broken and the seating is on the road edge, so it is a poor choice with a wheelchair or a small child.

name: The Fort Print Room
blurb: Two hours setting type by hand and pulling a print. Six people, ink on your hands, one colour or two.
description: A working letterpress shop: set metal type, lock the forme, ink, and pull prints on a Heidelberg. Six people at two benches, so it is genuinely hands-on rather than watching. No chance of a wheelchair at the press, and you will leave with ink under your nails. Two hours minimum, no short version.

name: The Basement Gallery, Kala Ghoda

hours.raw: Tu-Su 12:00-20:00 (opening nights are free, others are not)

blurb: A stone-walled cellar with six artists changing every month, and an opening on the last Friday. Thirteen steps down.
description: Bare stone walls, low light, and a changing group show. Entry is by donation and the room is genuinely underground, which is part of the draw. Thirteen steps and a turn; no lift and no alternative. Friday openings are crowded and the rest of the week it is nearly empty.

__meta.note: `hours.raw` is deliberately unparsable (a note in parentheses, which the adapter must reject) so the `hours_unverified` path is exercised by catalogue data, not only by a unit test.

name: Bombay Samachar Marg Print Gallery
blurb: Working letterpress museum with a glass wall onto the floor. You can watch type being set from four metres away.
description: A preserved print works on a lane off a street named after a newspaper, with viewing windows onto the working floor. The machines are run by printers who will explain what you are looking at if you ask. Level access, and it is five degrees cooler than the lane outside.

__meta.note: Modelled on the Fort print-trade lanes. Verify against the OSM snapshot; do not present the name as a real institution.

name: Fort Market Loom
blurb: Ninety minutes at a hand loom, making a cotton stole on a pit loom. Eight people, and the noise is considerable.
description: A working handloom room above a shop. You thread, treadle and weave a narrow cotton stole, which takes ninety minutes and is genuinely harder than it sounds. Stairs to the first floor with no lift, and the treadles are loud enough that a quiet room is not an option.

name: Sound of the Fort — ghazal and qawwali
blurb: Two hours of unamplified ghazal and qawwali in a hall off Fort's back streets. Cross-legged, on the floor.
description: Singers with no microphone to speak of, in a hall where the audience sits on the floor. The second hour is qawwali and the room changes character completely. Step-free at the door, flat throughout, and the floor seating is not adjustable for anyone who cannot sit cross-legged.

name: Kissa Corner, Fort lanes
blurb: Two hundred and fifty rupees, a steel chai counter, and a bench you can sit on with a laptop. Nobody will hurry you.
description: A tiny ground-floor room in an office lane, run by people who clearly stopped trying to be a cafe a long time ago. Omelette, bhaji, chai, and a shelf of old film posters. One step up into the room; the pavement outside is wide enough for two chairs.

__meta.note: `hours.status` is `absent` on purpose: the hours string was never surveyed, so the gate must reject with `hours_unverified` rather than assume it is open.

name: Karnataka Press building
blurb: A blue-and-white tiled facade on a busy corner, and half an hour is all it needs from you.
description: A late-nineteenth-century printing-office building with a tiled frontage and a carved facade, on a junction where four languages of signage compete. You look at it from the pavement; there is nothing to enter. Level, wide pavement, and a good place to stop and orient yourself.
